Southeast Asian foreign ministers convened ahead of a landmark ASEAN summit welcoming East Timor as its 11th member.

The meeting also precedes U.S. President Donald Trump's first trip to Asia since returning to the White House, with leaders set to address regional security and economic challenges amidst global political turbulence.
A new Miss USA has been crowned.
Audrey Eckert of Nebraska claimed the title of Miss USA 2025 at the 74th annual pageant held Friday night at the Grand Sierra Resort in Reno.
The 23-year-old was crowned by reigning Miss Universe, Victoria Kjær Theilvig.
Ontario Premier Doug Ford is pausing anti-tariff advertisements that angered U.S. President Donald Trump.
The ads, featuring former President Ronald Reagan, prompted Trump to halt trade talks with Canada.
Ford stated the campaign achieved its goal of initiating a conversation about tariffs.
The commercials will continue this weekend.
Canadian officials remain ready for talks to reduce tariffs in specific sectors.
The Atienza family faces profound grief following the sudden passing of 19-year-old Emmanuelle Atienza in Los Angeles.
This tragedy follows her sister Eliana's suspension from the University of Pennsylvania for pro-Palestine activism.
Eliana, a vocal advocate, faced backlash and temporary homelessness after her campus ban, highlighting a difficult period for the family.
Today, voters in Ireland go to the polls to elect a new president, with independent candidate Catherine Connolly leading the charge.
Her competitor, Heather Humphreys from the Fine Gael party, is keen to leverage her extensive governmental background.
While the presidential role is symbolic, Connolly has garnered substantial backing from left-leaning factions, presenting a spirited challenge.
The US government will defend its new $100,000 H-1B visa fee in court.
Officials state the system has been misused, harming American wages.
Lawsuits have been filed by business groups and others.
The fee applies to new petitions, aiming to tighten the visa system.
Indian nationals are a significant portion of H-1B recipients.
The University of Virginia has reached a compliance agreement with the Trump administration, halting a federal investigation into its admissions policies.

This deal requires the university to align its practices with the administration's interpretation of the Supreme Court's race-based admissions ban, in exchange for quarterly reports and continued federal funding.
A Chicago elementary school teacher, Lucy Martinez, faces backlash after a viral video showed her simulating an assassination during a protest.
The incident, captured by a passenger in a truck displaying a flag honoring Charlie Kirk, has led to calls for her dismissal.
The school has removed its online presence amid threats against Martinez.
Delhi Police have booked six Jawaharlal Nehru University students.
This action follows a protest march that led to a clash with police.
Three office-bearers of the students' union are among those booked.
The students were protesting against alleged attacks by ABVP members.
Police stated their action was to maintain order.
The JNU Teachers' Association condemned the police action.
White House officials met with university leaders to discuss the proposed Compact for Academic Excellence in Higher Education, which has faced rejections from several top institutions.
The compact requires universities to ban DEI programs and limit international students in exchange for federal funding.
The administration plans to revise the compact based on feedback.
Israel's Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered strong action against Hamas targets in Gaza.
This follows reports of Hamas violating a ceasefire.
The Rafah border crossing between Gaza and Egypt will remain closed.
This decision is linked to Hamas' handling of Israeli hostages' bodies.
Hamas accused Netanyahu of using pretexts to disrupt the ceasefire deal.
Thousands across the US participated in 'No Kings' protests, voicing concerns over President Trump's alleged authoritarian practices impacting constitutional rights.
Demonstrations, held in over 2,500 cities, aimed to foster greater political engagement.
Organizers encouraged participants to wear yellow, symbolizing unity and peaceful resistance in these nationwide movements.
This is the latest series of mass protests against the Trump administration.
Millions are set to protest across America on October 18, Saturday.
Organized by 'No Kings', the demonstrations aim to reject what organizers call authoritarianism.
Protests are planned in over 2,500 locations nationwide.
This event follows similar mass demonstrations in June.
Organizers aim to send a clear message of unity and democratic defense.
The "No Kings" protests are aimed at celebrating the 1st Amendment.
Trey Reed's death: A Black student's death at Delta State University, initially ruled a suicide, is now under scrutiny.
Family concerns and a private investigation, including an independent autopsy, have fueled allegations of a lynching and cover-up.
Activists are planning a protest today to demand accountability for the tragic incident.
Five universities were asked to join a White House call regarding President Trump's higher-education compact, with the University of Virginia declining to sign.

The compact asks colleges to align with Trump's political priorities for favorable research funding access, but has faced widespread rejection due to concerns over academic freedom and government interference.

New York City's mayoral race is dominated by Donald Trump's threats, with Democratic nominee Zohran Mamdani vowing to confront him while also offering to work on affordability.
His rival, Andrew Cuomo, adopts a more conciliatory approach, aiming to appeal to potential crossover voters by positioning himself as a liaison with the president.

Columbia Law School now requires international JD applicants to explain their reasons for studying in the U.S. This change follows a $220 million settlement with the federal government, which also mandates Columbia to reduce its reliance on international tuition.
Other Columbia schools are expected to implement similar application updates for future admissions cycles.
Harvard's student paper joins 43 others supporting a lawsuit challenging federal actions against noncitizens for political speech.
The case, filed by The Stanford Daily, argues the Trump administration violated the First Amendment by targeting pro-Palestine views, impacting campus journalism and international student expression.
Labor unions have filed a lawsuit alleging the Trump administration violated First Amendment rights by using AI to monitor social media for specific viewpoints, including criticism of Israel.
The complaint argues this surveillance program chills speech among visa holders and legal residents, threatening immigration action for expressing disapproved views.

Professor Adam Hanieh explains that the recent Israel-Palestine ceasefire is a misnomer, failing to address fundamental Palestinian rights and aiming to consolidate US dominance in the oil-rich Middle East.
He highlights the shift of oil exports to China, creating an 'East-East energy axis' and influencing global rivalries.
At least four North American airports experienced disruptions on Tuesday when unauthorized pro-Palestinian messages praising Hamas were broadcast.
Messages also targeted President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Incidents occurred at four airports.
Investigations are underway to ensure security and prevent future breaches.
Operations have since returned to normal.

Lahore protest today: Intense violence erupted in Lahore as Tehreek-i-Labbaik Pakistan (TLP) supporters clashed with police during a protest march towards Islamabad.
The unrest, which began last Thursday, escalated after the group was stopped, leading to fatalities and injuries on both sides.
The TLP vowed to continue its 'Gaza march' despite the crackdown and internet suspensions.

Australian Senator Lidia Thorpe faces investigation and widespread condemnation for remarks at a pro-Palestine rally, where she drew parallels between Palestinians and Indigenous Australians and spoke of potentially "burning down Parliament House." Thorpe clarified her comments were metaphorical, a figure of speech for pain and the need to end genocide.
The UK government is demanding stronger action from universities to protect Jewish students following a deadly synagogue attack and rising antisemitism concerns.
Education minister Bridget Phillipson stated universities must confront hate and division, with the government backing their use of powers to ensure campuses are safe spaces.
Israel’s latest Gaza ceasefire deal excludes Marwan Barghouti, the most popular Palestinian leader, from the list of around 250 prisoners to be released in exchange for hostages held by Hamas.

While Israel plans to free members of Hamas and Fatah jailed since the 2000s, Hamas insists on Barghouti’s release, viewing him as a unifying figure and potential successor to Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas.
Tens of thousands protested in Barcelona and Rome against Israel's Gaza campaign, fueled by the aid flotilla interception and Spain's strong diplomatic stance.

Spain's PM even labeled the destruction "genocide." Rome's rally, organized by Palestinian groups, also featured calls for a Palestinian state amidst controversial slogans, as Gaza's casualties mount.
The Trump administration has sent a 10-point memo to US colleges linking federal funding to caps on international students, tuition freezes, ideological screening, and diversity rules.
Rights groups warn the guidance threatens academic freedom.
Settlements with Columbia, Brown, and potential Harvard deals highlight the government’s crackdown on pro-Palestinian protests.
